title: Skimmed-prefetch dual-path rerank: reduce p95 latency and token work
creator: Tomás Rivera
description:
Problem: The reranker endpoint p95 latency and token cost spike when candidate sets are large or when long context KV cache misses occur. Current single-path scoring executes full-token scoring for every candidate which increases tail latency and unit cost for high-volume customers.

Proposal: Implement a two-stage 'skimmed-prefetch' pipeline plus a dual execution path inside the reranker service: (1) a lightweight, GPU-friendly skim model or heuristic prefilter that runs with micro-batched low-latency kernels to reduce candidate set (e.g., top-K from 100 -> 12), (2) a dual-path scoring engine that runs a short-circuit fast-path for tight deadlines (prefix-only, quantized kernels, early-exit when score delta exceeds margin) and a full-accuracy path for normal budgets. Combine with proactive KV-cache prefetch for predicted hot sequences and deadline-aware microbatching that enforces per-request token caps and soft timeouts.

Design trade-offs: Prefilter reduces quality risk vs cost — we'll tune prefilter recall target to 98% measured on held-out rerank testsets. The fast-path introduces approximate scoring (quantized kernels + truncated decoding) with a configurable fallback to full path if uncertainty is high. This adds complexity to routing and telemetry but minimizes impact to users because fallbacks happen only on uncertain examples.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 endpoint latency improvement >= 28% on 99th percentile heavy-candidate traces (internal benchmark).
- Median token cost per request reduced >= 22% for top-10k customer traces.
- Quality regression <= 0.6% NDCG@10 on production prompt set.
- No increase in error rate or 5xxs post-rollout.

Plan:
1) Implement prefilter as a lightweight Transformer distilled to 1/6 size or a sparse ANN heuristic behind a feature flag (ENG branch).
2) Add dual-path scoring interface with deadline signal for fast-path short-circuit and per-request token limit enforcement.
3) KV-cache prefetch hook: predict top prefixes from recent traffic and prewarm device cache asynchronously.
4) Add metrics: per-request path taken, prefilter recall, fast-path fallback rate, token usage per path, latency shards.
5) Canary rollout to low-traffic tenants then percentage ramp with automatic rollback on error or quality drift.

Rollout signal thresholds: fallback_rate > 6% for more than 30m OR NDCG@10 drop > 0.8% OR 5xx delta +0.2% -> rollback.
